description: A nation east of the Jordan descended from Lot's younger son Ben-ammi (Genesis 19:36-38), frequently hostile to Israel. Jephthah defeated Ammonite forces oppressing Israel (Judges 10-11), and Ammon's king Hanun's humiliation of David's envoys sparked a war (2 Samuel 10). Ammonite officials like Tobiah later opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:3).
family_friendly_summary: Ammon was a nation east of the Jordan River, descended from Lot's family, and often an enemy of Israel. The judge Jephthah defeated an Ammonite army that was troubling God's people, and later King David fought a war with Ammon after their king insulted the messengers David had sent in kindness.
